question: What is the full pipeline from capturing images/LiDAR of a physical space to creating an immersive web-based 3D environment using Gaussian splatting and hybrid mesh+splat techniques? How do you extract meshes from splat scenes? What hybrid rendering approaches exist? How does LiDAR fit in?
executive_summary: The optimal pipeline uses a dual-branch architecture: COLMAP sparse reconstruction feeds both 3DGS splat training (for photorealistic appearance) and a separate mesh generation path (for structural geometry), combined in a WebGPU viewer via depth-composited hybrid rendering. iPhone/iPad LiDAR via Scaniverse provides the fastest single-tool path to both mesh and splat from one capture session. Mesh extraction from Gaussians is possible via SuGaR, 2DGS, or GOF, but traditional photogrammetry (Meshroom/OpenMVS) produces better-topology meshes for the structural layer. All extracted meshes require significant post-processing (decimation to 100K-300K triangles, format conversion to GLB with Draco compression) before web deployment. Hybrid rendering is supported by PlayCanvas, Three.js, and Babylon.js v9 using a standard depth compositing pattern.

key_findings.finding: Dual-branch pipeline (COLMAP to both 3DGS splats and photogrammetry mesh) produces the best hybrid result, with both branches sharing coordinate systems automatically
iPhone/iPad LiDAR via Scaniverse produces both mesh and splat from a single capture session in the same coordinate frame, with SPZ format reducing splat size 90%
Four mesh extraction methods exist (SuGaR, 2DGS, GOF, DN-Splatter) but all produce meshes with more artifacts and worse topology than traditional photogrammetry
Hybrid mesh+splat rendering uses depth compositing (mesh writes depth, splats depth-test-only) and is supported by PlayCanvas, Three.js (GaussianSplats3D, dvt3d/splat-mesh), and Babylon.js v9
Raw extracted meshes are NOT web-ready: they require 5-20x decimation, UV unwrapping for some methods, and GLB conversion with Draco compression for web delivery
KHR_gaussian_splatting glTF extension (ratified August 2025) enables storing splat data alongside mesh geometry in a single container; Cesium supports it as of March 2026
Texture baking from Gaussian appearance to UV atlas produces washed-out colors, reinforcing the value of hybrid rendering where splats handle visual fidelity

open_questions: How to solve washed-out texture baking from Gaussians for mesh-only fallback rendering
What is the optimal boundary between mesh and splat content in a hybrid scene
Progressive loading strategies for combined mesh+splat assets in large environments
Mobile WebGPU performance budgets for combined mesh+splat rendering
contradictions: H1 implies mesh extraction produces usable output while H6 shows significant post-processing is required before web deployment
